column3: NASB follows the critical text (“some elders”); “an orator” is rendered “a certain attorney,” and “made a representation” is “brought charges.”
NASB follows the critical text (“reforms”); it adds “Paul” and “to the governor” and renders “foresight” as “providence.”
NASB renders “gladly accept” as “acknowledge.”
NASB renders “be a hindrance” as “weary” and “hear us briefly” as “grant us … a brief hearing.”
NASB follows the critical text (“dissension”); it adds “real” and “a fellow” and renders “leader” as “ringleader.”
NASB prints the Textus Receptus words beginning “And we wanted to judge him” in braces, continuing through v. 8a.
NASB prints this Textus Receptus verse in braces.

NASB keeps the Textus Receptus words “ordering his accusers to come before you” inside the braces; the rest follows the critical text, with “to know” rendered “to ascertain.” A stray quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text; “agreed” is rendered “joined in the attack.”
NASB follows the critical text; “signalling” is rendered “nodded,” and “encouraging” is “cheerfully.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text (“twelve”); “to know” is rendered “take note of the fact.”
NASB follows the critical text; “making an obstruction of a crowd” is rendered “causing a riot,” and it reorders the verse.
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB follows the critical text; “confess” is rendered “admit,” and “the ancestral God” is “the God of our fathers.”
NASB follows the critical text without “of the dead”; “await” is rendered “cherish,” and “the unjust” is “the wicked.”
NASB follows the critical text; “strive” is rendered “do my best,” and “through all” is “always.”
NASB renders “many years” as “several years.”
NASB follows the critical text; it moves “But there were certain Jews from Asia,” which opens v. 19 in the Greek, into this verse, and renders “purified” as “occupied … having been purified.”
NASB begins after the phrase moved to v. 18; it follows the critical text.
NASB follows the critical text without “if” and “in me”; “unrighteousness” is rendered “misdeed.”
NASB follows the critical text; “I am judged” is rendered “I am on trial.” A stray quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text without “having heard these things”; “deferred” is rendered “put … off,” and “I will examine the things as to you” is “I will decide your case.”
NASB follows the critical text without “or to come to him”; “ease” is rendered “some freedom.”
NASB follows the critical text (“his wife,” “Christ Jesus”).
NASB follows the critical text; “opportunity” is rendered “time.”
NASB follows the critical text without “that he might release him”; “riches” is rendered “money.”
NASB follows the critical text; “to acquire favor with” is rendered “to do … a favor.”
